alex: quick head-to-head run: L4 vs T4 vs A10G for embeddings (512-d) and small-chat (ctx=128, 1-shot). regions tested: us-central1, europe-west1, asia-east1. tl;dr: L4 best $/embed, A10G best p95/p99 for small-chat, T4 cheapest hourly but tail latency and kernel variance in eu is rough.

alex: raw summary table (p95 small-chat ms, p99 ms, embeds qps, cost per 1M tokens USD):
```
gpu,region,smallchat_p95_ms,smallchat_p99_ms,embeds_qps,cost_per_1M_tokens
A10G,us-central1,48,92,920,4.1
L4,us-central1,62,130,1450,2.6
T4,us-central1,110,290,980,1.8
A10G,europe-west1,52,110,880,4.4
L4,europe-west1,70,190,1320,2.9
T4,europe-west1,140,420,860,1.9
A10G,asia-east1,58,125,760,4.9
L4,asia-east1,78,210,1120,3.4
T4,asia-east1,160,480,700,2.2
```

bench-bot: automated plots uploaded: https://artifacts.internal/bench/2312345678/plots.zip :bar_chart:

priya: nice. can you share kernel choices / quantization used for these numbers? was kv-cache fused, and are we on int8 fp16 mixes?

alex: baseline = fp16, non-fused kv (stock kernels). then ran int8 quant sweep with our lz4-backed cache on. int8 used OPT-quant pipeline + per-channel calibration. results below.

marco: short notes on quant sweep: int8 on L4 -> +34% embed qps, small-chat p95 ~ +5ms (slightly worse) overall quality drop ~0.6% cosine on nist-200 subset. int8 on T4 -> +28% qps but p99 spikes more frequently in eu. A10G int8 -> +18% qps, p95 improved slightly vs fp16 (weird), quality delta ~0.4%.

claire: curious — how did you measure quality? what thresholds for rolling this to dedicated?

marco: eval set = 5k embed pairs (NIST + internal), cosine drop measured; chat eval = 1k prompts w/ human labels for coherence (A/B). threshold we use: <=1% embed cosine drop AND no >10% regressions on chat acceptability. int8 passes for L4 on embeddings but borderline for chat.

alex: capacity planning snippet (approx requests/sec per GPU, mixed workload 70% embeds / 30% small-chat):
```
gpu,approx_reqs_per_gpu_mixed
L4,720 req/s (peak sustained)
A10G,520 req/s
T4,460 req/s
```
pricing notes: used cloud list rates + reserved discounts: effective $/hour used for cost_per_1M_tokens above.

priya: any kernel-specific tips? I remember a fused kv kernel landed last month. did you try it?

alex: yes - fused-kv + custom attention tiling helps small-chat tail on L4 and A10G (p99 down ~18% on L4, ~12% on A10G). on T4 fused-kv reduces avg latency but increases variance in eu due to driver/context churn. so recommendation: enable fused-kv for L4/A10G in prod, leave off for T4 unless you have heavy batching and strict driver tuning.

marco: one extra datapoint: cold-starts (kv/cache miss heavy) blow up T4 p99 to 900ms in asia under bursty traffic; L4 stays ~280ms, A10G ~210ms. caching strategy + warm pools helped the most.

claire: operational ask — can you add a simple runbook: if p99>250ms, fallback to A10G pool or reduce batch size? also note region failover.

alex: added to backlog. quick command we used to reproduce (internal harness):
```bash
./run_bench --model small-chat-v1 --gpu L4 --region us-central1 --kernels fused_kv=false --quant fp16 --qps 800 --ctx 128
./run_bench --model embed-512 --gpu L4 --region us-central1 --quant int8 --qps 1200
```

bench-bot: regression alert: int8-chat-eval drop 0.9% on sample_202603 -> flagged, see /evals/2312345678/int8-chat-report.json

priya: thanks — this helps a lot. proposal: L4 int8 for embeddings (prod), keep small-chat on A10G (fp16 with fused-kv) and T4 as overflow/burst with strict warm-pools and region exclusions for eu for now.

alex: agree. will draft rollout plan + canary config (5% traffic to L4-int8 embeddings, 95% to A10G fp16 chat) and post in #eng-platform. :thumbsup:
